name: HALoGEN
description: A comprehensive hallucination evaluation framework generating approximately 150,000 model outputs from 14 LLMs across 9 generation settings (biography, scientific claim, news, etc.). Introduces a three-type error taxonomy: incorrect recollection (the model misremembers real information), training data errors (hallucinations inherited from training data), and fabrication (entirely invented information). Even the best models hallucinate up to 86% of atomic facts in some high-hallucination domains.
evaluation_method: hallucination rate (atomic fact verification via search/knowledge bases)
general_score_metric: hallucination rate (% atomic facts hallucinated; lower is better)
typical_sota_score: 10–86% hallucination rate depending on domain (biography and scientific claims show highest rates)
reputation: Published at ACL 2025; from Allen Institute for AI and University of Washington; one of the most comprehensive hallucination benchmarks to date; systematic across 14 models and 9 settings
notes: ACL 2025. Three-type taxonomy distinguishes hallucination causes — crucial for mitigation strategies since different causes require different fixes. Automated verification pipeline using search engines and knowledge bases enables scalable evaluation. Finding: top models still hallucinate significant portions of atomic facts in knowledge-intensive generation tasks. From Allen Institute for AI.
